name: MovingAverageGapBar
quote: moving average gap bar (gap bar): A bar that does not touch the moving average. The space between the bar and the moving average is the gap.
description: Shared primitive: the current bar's low is above the EMA (long) / high is below the EMA (short) -- the bar does not touch the 20-bar EMA.

complexity.reason: needs an EMA

notes: The first MA gap bar in a strong trend's pullback is a described buy/sell setup for a test of the trend extreme (R00-53 second-setup variant).

name: TwentyMovingAverageGapBars
quote: 20 moving average gap bars: Twenty or more consecutive bars that have not touched the moving average. Once the market finally touches the moving average, it usually creates a setup for a test of the trend's extreme.
description: At least N consecutive bars have all been moving-average gap bars in the same direction -- a strong-trend context filter; once the streak ends (a bar finally touches the EMA), a test of the trend extreme is expected.

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop of an EMA-relative test

name: SecondMovingAverageGapBarSetup
quote: second moving average gap bar setup: If there is a first moving average gap bar and a reversal toward the moving average does not reach the moving average, and instead the move away from the moving average continues, it is the next reversal in the direction of the moving average gap.
description: After a first MovingAverageGapBar, if the subsequent pullback toward the EMA fails to reach it and price resumes away from the EMA, the next reversal back toward the EMA is the qualifying (second) setup.
book_order_type: n/a (context classification enabling the qualifying reversal entry)

complexity.reason: needs the first gap-bar event and its subsequent failed-pullback state retained across bars

name: NoConsecutiveClosesOppositeEma
quote: No two consecutive trend bar closes occur on the opposite side of the moving average.
description: Filter: over the last N bars, no two consecutive trend-bar closes fell on the opposite side of the EMA from the prevailing trend -- a strong-trend confirmation (bull: no two consecutive closes both below the EMA).
pseudocode: for i in 0..lookback-2: !(R00-01[i] && close[i] < ema(emaLength)[i] && R00-01[i+1] && close[i+1] < ema(emaLength)[i+1])

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop combining the trend-bar primitive with an EMA

name: NearEmaAugmentsReversalOdds
quote: especially when the bar is at the moving average in a bull trend.
description: Filter: the failed-bear-breakout confirmation (R01-07) is more reliable when the confirming bar sits at or near the EMA.

complexity.reason: needs an EMA and an ATR-scaled distance band

chapter_title: Example of How to Trade a Breakout

name: MovingAverageGapBar
quote: Bar 12 was a second-entry moving average gap bar short setup ... It had a bear body and was also a 20-gap bar short setup
description: Shared primitive: a bar whose entire range sits on one side of the EMA without touching it — used as evidence of countertrend strength and as a stand-alone signal bar for second-entry setups.
book_order_type: sell stop below the gap bar's low (short case)

complexity.reason: needs an EMA plus a whole-bar comparison against it

notes: ‘Second entry’ and ‘20-gap bar’ are named but not defined in this chapter; the ranges book's own chapters on first-moving-average gap bars and 20-gap bars (outside the mining scope here) should supply the full definitions.
chapter_title: Example of How to Trade a Breakout

name: NoCloseBelowEmaForNBars
quote: there had not yet been a close below the moving average and the market had been above the moving average for more than 20 bars, both of which are signs of strength.
description: Sign of strength: no bar has closed below the EMA for at least N bars — evidence the trend remains strong.

complexity.reason: an EMA plus a fixed-length existence scan for any violation

chapter_title: Breakout Entries in Existing Strong Trends

name: FirstCloseBelowEmaTwoBarReversalInsideBar
quote: Bar 9 was a bull inside bar after the first close below the moving average and the second bar of a two-bar reversal, so a breakout above the setup was expected to test the bull high at a minimum.
description: In a bull trend that has just posted its first close below the EMA in a long time, a two-bar reversal (down then up) whose second bar is a bull inside bar is a buy setup targeting at least the trend high.
pseudocode: close[2] >= ema(emaLength)[2] && close[1] < ema(emaLength)[1] && close[1] < open[1] && high[0] < high[1] && low[0] > low[1]
book_order_type: buy stop above the inside bar's high

complexity.reason: combines an EMA-crossing state test with a two-bar reversal and an inside-bar pattern

chapter_title: Breakout Entries in Existing Strong Trends

name: FirstEmaGapBarShortEntry
quote: if there is a strong bear trend and the market finally rallies above the moving average, the first bar in that rally that has a low above the moving average is a first moving average gap bar. Traders will place a sell stop order at one tick below the low of that bar to go short
description: In a bear trend, the first bar of a countertrend rally whose low closes above the EMA is a 'first moving average gap bar'; sell one tick below its low, trailing the stop down to one tick below each new bar's low until filled.
pseudocode: isFirstBarWithLowAboveEma = low[0] > ema(emaLength) && low[1] <= ema(emaLength)[1]; onceTriggered, entryStopLevel = min(entryStopLevel, low[0]) each bar until filled
book_order_type: sell stop, trailed down one tick below each subsequent bar's low until filled

complexity.reason: a persistent, ratcheting pending-order level carried across bars, not a single-bar stop test

notes: Related to R08-25 (EmaGapBarAsCountertrendStrength), which uses the same EMA-gap-bar concept as a filter rather than an entry trigger.

name: SecondEmaGapBarRetryEntry
quote: Sometimes they will get stopped out by the market moving above the signal bar, and if that happens, they will try one more time to reenter their shorts at one tick below the low of the prior bar. Once filled, the signal bar is a second moving average gap bar short signal.
description: If the R06-09 short is stopped out, re-enter short one tick below the low of the next qualifying bar (a second EMA gap bar).
book_order_type: sell stop below the second signal bar's low

complexity.reason: needs the prior trade's stopped-out state remembered across bars, plus the EMA

name: EmaGapReversalFadeInRange
quote: if it then sells off to below the moving average but is followed by a strong bull reversal bar with a high that is below the moving average, traders will often go long above that bar if there enough room between the high of that bar and the moving average for a long scalp
description: In a trading-range day, after price dips below the EMA and a strong bull reversal bar closes with its high still below the EMA, buy above that bar for a scalp back to the EMA, provided enough room remains.
pseudocode: high[0] < ema(emaLength) && bullReversalBar[0] && (ema(emaLength) - high[0]) >= minScalpTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal bar

complexity.reason: EMA plus a single-bar reversal test and a room-to-target check

name: EmaGapBarAsCountertrendStrength
quote: since there had yet to be a sharp rally (like a gap bar above the exponential moving average), countertrend trades had to be scalps
description: Filter: allow a countertrend swing (long in a bear trend) only if within the last N bars a bar formed entirely above the EMA (a moving-average gap bar).

complexity.reason: EMA plus a window scan

notes: Without it, countertrend trades are scalps only (or skipped).
chapter_title: Measured Moves Based on Gaps and Trading Ranges

name: ReversalOnlyAtKeyTechnicalConfluence
quote: it is important to watch for these patterns when the market is at key technical levels, like at measured move targets, trend lines, and even higher time frame moving averages and trend lines
description: Filter: only treat a reversal pattern as high-probability when it forms at a remembered magnet level (measured-move target, trend line, higher-time-frame moving average or trend line), not in the open middle of a move.

complexity.reason: 'nearestMagnetLevel' is a design decision -- which of the many magnet families (measured move, trend line, higher-timeframe MA) is on offer is not specified

notes: Generalizes R08-14/R08-15's measured-move-specific gating to any magnet family; see Chapter 10 for the fuller magnet list.
chapter_title: Reversals Often End at Signal Bars from Prior Failed Reversals

name: MovingAverageTouchGapBarSetup
quote: A bar touches the moving average (a 20 gap bar buy setup).
description: The current bar's low touches or dips into the 20-bar EMA after a pullback, a classic support test (the '20 gap bar' setup, developed fully in Chapter 13).
pseudocode: low[0] <= ema(emaLength)[0] && low[0] >= ema(emaLength)[0] - touchTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: buy stop above the touch bar's high

complexity.reason: needs the EMA plus a touch-tolerance test

chapter_title: First Pullback Sequence: Bar, Minor Trend Line, Moving Average, Moving Average Gap, Major Trend Line

name: CloseBelowMovingAverage
quote: A bar has a close below the moving average.
description: Stage marker: a bar closes below the 20-bar EMA in an established bull trend, deeper than a mere touch.

complexity.reason: single EMA comparison

chapter_title: First Pullback Sequence: Bar, Minor Trend Line, Moving Average, Moving Average Gap, Major Trend Line

name: MovingAverageGapBar
quote: A bar has a high below the moving average (a moving average gap bar).
description: Shared primitive: the entire bar (its high, not just the close) sits below the 20-bar EMA -- a moving-average gap bar, a materially deeper sign of weakness than CloseBelowMovingAverage.
book_order_type: n/a (context signal, often the first leg toward a major trend-line break)

complexity.reason: single EMA comparison

notes: Same construction as R08-25's EmaGapBarAsCountertrendStrength; here it is one stage in a bull trend's own weakening sequence rather than a countertrend-permission filter.
chapter_title: First Pullback Sequence: Bar, Minor Trend Line, Moving Average, Moving Average Gap, Major Trend Line

name: MaTouchFailureExpectsDeeperPullback
quote: If the market cannot move above the moving average after about 10 to 20 bars, it is probably because traders want more of a discount before aggressively buying. The result is that the market will have to fall further before enough buyers return to lift the market up to test the old highs.
description: Filter: once price has failed to reclaim the EMA within N bars of touching it, withhold with-trend long entries and expect a deeper pullback before the old high is tested.

complexity.reason: needs the persisted bar count since the MA was first touched

chapter_title: First Pullback Sequence: Bar, Minor Trend Line, Moving Average, Moving Average Gap, Major Trend Line

name: IncreasingMovingAveragePenetrationAcrossPullbacks
quote: Compare the bars 4, 5, and 8 tests of the moving average and notice that bar 5 penetrated it more than bar 4, and bar 8 had more penetration than bar 5. This is to be expected, and when this is the case be careful about placing a short trade, because there will be many smart bears who will short only at a higher price, and many bulls who will be confident enough to buy dips.
description: Filter: if each successive pullback penetrates the moving average more deeply than the last, be cautious about fading (countertrend) that penetration -- successive with-trend traders are buying dips more confidently and countertrend entries there carry more risk.

complexity.reason: needs the depth of the prior EMA-touch to persist across bars for comparison

chapter_title: First Pullback Sequence: Bar, Minor Trend Line, Moving Average, Moving Average Gap, Major Trend Line

name: HigherTimeframeSequentialMovingAveragePullback
quote: there is often a tendency for the first pullback to the 15 minute moving average to be followed by a test of the trend extreme, and then a pullback to the 30 or 60 minute moving average, which would likely be followed by another test of the extreme.
description: Higher-timeframe EMAs (15/30/60 minute) act as a sequence of successively larger magnets: the first pullback to reach a given higher-timeframe EMA is usually followed by a trend-extreme test, then the next pullback tests the next-larger timeframe's EMA.
pseudocode: close[0] within touchTicks of higherTfEma(emaLength, timeframeMinutes)[0]

complexity.reason: needs a design decision on whether/how the engine exposes a resampled higher-timeframe EMA, same as R10-16

notes: Brooks: not worth the effort on lower timeframes generally, but the tendency exists; kept low-confidence.
chapter_title: First Pullback Sequence: Bar, Minor Trend Line, Moving Average, Moving Average Gap, Major Trend Line

name: TwentyGapBarSetup
quote: When the market stays on one side of the moving average without touching it for 20 consecutive bars or more, the trend is strong, but it is also overdone and will likely soon pull back to the moving average.
description: Shared primitive: a persistent counter of consecutive bars whose high-low range has not touched the N-bar EMA; the setup is armed once the counter reaches a threshold.
pseudocode: barsSinceEmaTouch = (low[0] <= ema(emaLength) && ema(emaLength) <= high[0]) ? 0 : barsSinceEmaTouch[1] + 1; barsSinceEmaTouch >= gapBarThreshold
book_order_type: n/a (context/state precondition, not itself an order)

complexity.reason: EMA plus a persistent streak counter of consecutive non-touch bars

notes: Brooks says 20 is arbitrary ('you can arbitrarily pick any large number of bars'); kept as the book's own default.
Brooks's '2HM' (two hours from the moving average) is a time-based alias for the same concept on a 5 minute chart, not a separate rule.

name: MovingAverageGapBarPrimitive
quote: there will likely be a test that goes through the moving average and forms a moving average gap bar where the bar is completely on the other side of the moving average so that there is a gap between the bar and the moving average.
description: Shared primitive: in a bull trend, the bar's entire range sits below the EMA (no overlap) -- the bar has crossed fully through and past the moving average.

complexity.reason: a single EMA value compared against the bar's high; no window loop or persistent state

notes: Redefined more generally (without the 20-gap-bar precondition) in chapter 14's R14-01.

name: FirstGapBarFadeEntry
quote: Look to fade the first gap bar (in a bull trend, buy one tick above the high of the previous bar if the high is below the exponential moving average).
description: After a 20-gap-bar setup, the first moving-average gap bar triggers a with-trend fade: buy one tick above its high, betting the trend resumes toward its prior extreme.
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the high of the gap bar

complexity.reason: composes a moderate streak-counter primitive with a simple EMA test; no new loop needed

notes: Swing part of the position per the book's advice; sizing itself is rejected below as discretion.

name: SecondGapBarFadeEntry
quote: If the first entry fails, buy again on the second entry, if there is one.
description: If the first gap-bar fade entry fails (stops out without the market testing the trend's prior extreme), take the next moving-average gap bar occurrence the same way, as a second attempt.
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the high of the second gap bar

complexity.reason: needs a persistent attempt counter that increments on each failed fade and resets once the trend's extreme is tested or a new trend forms

notes: Same 'count to two, then stop' structure as the high/low 1-4 bar counting formalized in chapter 17.

name: NoThirdGapBarFadeFilter
quote: it is not worth buying a third time if the first two setups fail since the market at that point is likely in a channel and not forming a reversal.
description: Block a third consecutive gap-bar fade attempt after two have already failed; treat the market as forming a channel rather than a with-trend bounce.

complexity.reason: reads the same persistent attempt counter as R13-04

name: GapBarAfterTrendReversalFailFilter
quote: if the first moving average gap bar forms after a strong trend reversal, it will likely fail because the trend has now reversed and that gap bar is a setup for the prior trend, which now has ended.
description: Suppress the moving-average gap-bar fade if a strong trend-direction reversal has just occurred; the gap bar belongs to the prior, now-ended trend.

complexity.reason: depends on a trend-direction-flip primitive (the AlwaysInDirection family) that is itself a design decision

name: MovingAverageGapBarGeneral
quote: if the high of a bar is below the moving average, then there is a gap between that bar and the moving average.
description: Shared primitive: in a bull trend or sideways market, the bar's entire range sits below the EMA (no overlap). Same test as chapter 13's R13-02, redefined here without any 20-bar no-touch precondition.

complexity.reason: a single EMA value compared against the bar's high; no window loop or persistent state

notes: Identical primitive to R13-02; expected to merge in dedup.

name: FirstMovingAverageGapBarSwingEntry
quote: if there is a strong bull and it finally has a bar that has a high below the moving average and then the next bar trades above the high of that bar, the market will try to form a higher high or lower high test of the bull's extreme.
description: In a strong trend, the first gap bar (R14-01) since the trend began sets up a swing buy one tick above its high, targeting a test of the trend's prior extreme.
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the gap bar's high, held for a swing target near the trend's prior extreme

complexity.reason: needs 'first since trend start' bookkeeping plus a trend-strength read (the AlwaysInDirection family) before the gap-bar test is trustworthy

notes: Same underlying gap-bar-breakout mechanism as R13-03, without the 20-bar no-touch precondition.

name: SecondAttemptGapBarEntry
quote: If the market again goes above the high of a prior bar, this is a second moving average gap bar setup, or a second attempt to fill a moving average gap in a bull trend, and the odds are excellent that there will be a tradable rally off this setup.
description: If a first gap-bar attempt does not hold and the pullback continues, the next bar whose high exceeds the prior bar's high while still below the EMA is a higher-confidence second entry.
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the second gap bar's high

complexity.reason: a persistent attempt counter incremented on each failed first attempt

notes: Same structure as R13-04; this file's version has no 20-gap-bar precondition.

name: ScalpVsSwingStrengthFilter
quote: So if there is a strong trend, a first moving average gap tends to set up swing trades, and if there is not a strong trend and a trader takes a moving average gap bar trade, she is more likely looking for a scalp.
description: Classify a gap-bar entry's intended objective (swing toward the trend extreme vs. a scalp back to the EMA) based on whether the trend is strong.
pseudocode: strongTrend() -> targetMode = SWING (trend extreme); else targetMode = SCALP (moving average)

complexity.reason: 'strong trend' is a design decision left to the AlwaysInDirection / trend-strength primitives defined elsewhere

name: InsufficientRoomToEmaFilter
quote: A trader will take the trade only if there is enough room to the moving average to make an acceptable profit
description: Block a scalp-style gap-bar fade if the distance from the current close to the EMA is below a minimum tick threshold.

complexity.reason: a single EMA distance compared against a fixed tick threshold

notes: Brooks gives no numeric minimum; minScalpTicks is a reading of 'enough room ... to make an acceptable profit.'

name: FlatMovingAverageFilter
quote: The moving average is relatively flat.
description: A trading-range clue: the moving average's slope over the last few bars is close to zero (neither clearly rising nor falling).
pseudocode:
maSlope = movingAverage[0] - movingAverage[maSlopeLookback];
isFlatMovingAverage = abs(maSlope) <= flatMaThreshold;
book_order_type: n/a (regime clue, one input to RP4-01)

complexity.reason: an EMA plus a simple lagged-difference slope test; the flatness cutoff has no stated numeric value

name: TradingRangeMajoritySideOfEmaFilter
quote: One very good rule is that if there is a trading range setting up and it is near the moving average, never look to buy if the bars are mostly below the moving average, and never look to sell if the bars are mostly above the moving average... when barbwire forms adjacent to the moving average, it will usually break out in the direction away from the moving average.
description: While a trading range/barbwire is forming near the 20-bar EMA, only allow entries in the direction implied by which side of the EMA most of the pattern's bars sit on: block longs when most bars are below the EMA, block shorts when most are above it.

complexity.reason: an EMA plus a bar-majority count over the pattern window

notes: Brooks states this twice in the chapter (once generally, once specifically for barbwire adjacent to the EMA); one candidate covers both statements.

name: FirstMovingAverageGapPullbackEntry
quote: If there is a strong trend, be ready for... the first moving average gap pullback.
description: In a strong trend, the first pullback that leaves a gap between price and the moving average (i.e., the pullback does not touch the average) is itself a qualifying reason.
book_order_type: n/a (counted as one of the 'reasons' in R26-01)

complexity.reason: needs an EMA distance test and a persistent since-trend-start counter of qualifying pullbacks

notes: Likely duplicates the moving-average gap-bar primitives from ranges chapter 13 (13_twenty_gap_bars.json); recorded here since this chapter names it as a distinct 'reason'.
chapter_title: Need Two Reasons to Take a Trade

name: FirstMovingAveragePullbackEntry
quote: if there is a strong trend, be ready for the first moving average pullback, for any two-legged pullbacks to the moving average
description: In a strong trend, the first pullback that actually touches the moving average (the first MA touch of the trend, or the first in more than N bars) is itself a qualifying reason.
pseudocode:
touchesMovingAverage = low[0] <= movingAverage[0] && high[0] >= movingAverage[0]; // long-side touch test
reasonPresent = touchesMovingAverage && barsSinceLastMovingAverageTouch >= minGapBars;
book_order_type: n/a (counted as one of the 'reasons' in R26-01)

complexity.reason: needs an EMA touch test and a persistent bars-since-last-touch counter

notes: The 'first in more than 20 bars' detail comes from the chapter's worked example (bar 2, Figure 26.1), used here as the default minGapBars.
chapter_title: Need Two Reasons to Take a Trade

name: QuietFlagMALimitEntry
quote: Buy at or below the prior bar on a limit order in a quiet bull flag at the moving average.
description: In a quiet bull flag pausing at the moving average, place a buy-limit order at or below the prior bar's low.
pseudocode:
limitPrice = low[0];
enterLongOnLimitNextBar = isQuietBullFlag[0] && isAtMovingAverage[0] && low[1] <= limitPrice;
book_order_type: buy limit order at or below the prior bar's low

complexity.reason: 'quiet' flag (a low-volatility/small-range qualifier on the flag primitive) is a design decision

name: QuietFlagMACloseEntry
quote: Buy a bear close in a quiet bull flag at the moving average.
description: In a quiet bull flag pausing at the moving average, buy the close of any bar that closes bearish.
pseudocode:
isBearCloseBar = close[0] < open[0];
enterLongAtClose = isQuietBullFlag[0] && isAtMovingAverage[0] && isBearCloseBar;
book_order_type: buy at the close of the bar

complexity.reason: same 'quiet flag' design decision as R28-27

name: MovingAverageGapBar
quote: A bar that does not touch the moving average.
description: A gap bar's low sits above (bull) / high sits below (bear) the 20-bar EMA, i.e. the whole bar clears the moving average with a gap.

complexity.reason: requires an EMA series, not just fixed-offset price arithmetic

notes: The first pullback in a strong trend that produces one of these is called out by Brooks as often setting up a test of the trend's extreme; see V00-14 for the 20-in-a-row escalation.
chapter_title: Front Matter: List of Terms and Introduction

name: TwentyMovingAverageGapBars
quote: Twenty or more consecutive bars that have not touched the moving average.
description: N or more consecutive moving-average gap bars (same side) is called out as a sign of a strong, persistent trend.

complexity.reason: a persistent counter of consecutive same-side gap bars, built on the EMA-gap primitive

name: NoStraddleAcrossMovingAverage
quote: No two consecutive trend bar closes occur on the opposite side of the moving average.
description: In a strong trend, no two consecutive trend-bar closes straddle the EMA (one above, one below) - a context filter for trend strength.
pseudocode: !((close[0] > ema[0]) != (close[1] > ema[1]) && close[0] != open[0] && close[1] != open[1])

name: WithTrendMajorityFilter
quote: If most of the past 10 or 20 bars are above the moving average, trend setups and trades are likely on the buy side.
description: A with-trend context gate: most of the last N bars closed above (long) / below (short) the 20-bar EMA.
pseudocode: countIf(close[i] > ema[i], i in 0..lookback-1) >= majorityFraction * lookback

complexity.reason: a counting loop against the EMA over a window

chapter_title: Front Matter: List of Terms and Introduction

name: SecondMovingAverageGapBarSetup
quote: If there is a first moving average gap bar and a reversal toward the moving average does not reach the moving average, and instead the move away from the moving average continues, it is the next reversal in the direction of the moving average.
description: After a first moving-average gap bar, if the following pullback toward the EMA fails to reach it and the trend resumes, the next EMA-gap-bar reversal setup is a 'second' setup with the same logic.
book_order_type: stop entry one tick beyond the setup bar

complexity.reason: needs to remember a prior gap-bar event and whether the subsequent pullback reached the EMA, cross-bar state beyond a simple counter

name: PullbackReachesEma
quote: The sell-off below bar 3 lasted only one bar and did not even reach the moving average.
description: A countertrend move is only significant enough to matter if it actually trades through the N-bar EMA; a pullback that stops short of the EMA does not qualify as a real test.

name: MovingAverageGapBarEntry
quote: a third entry for a moving average gap bar long (its high was below the moving average and it was the first pullback after the strong rally to bar 10)
description: Primitive: a pullback bar whose entire range stays on the far side of the EMA (its high stays below the EMA during a bull pullback) signals strong trend resumption and is bought.

name: CloseAboveEmaByMargin
quote: The spike goes very far and breaks several resistance levels like the moving average, prior swing highs, and trend lines, and each by many ticks.
description: The close is above the N-bar EMA by at least a margin (in ticks).

complexity.reason: needs an EMA

notes: CloseAboveAverage has no margin and uses a simple average.

name: PullbackHoldsAboveEma
quote: The pullback that tests the bear low fails at the moving average or the old bear trend line.
description: The pullback's lowest low over the last N bars stayed at or above the EMA (within a tolerance) and this bar closes up - the moving average held as support.
pseudocode: lowest(low, pullbackBars, 0) >= ema(emaLen) - toleranceTicks * tick && close[0] > open[0] && close[1] < close[pullbackBars]
book_order_type: buy stop above the bar that holds the average

complexity.reason: EMA plus a window lowest

name: TrendLineBreakReachesEma
quote: If the break of the trend line is not even strong enough to reach the moving average, it is usually not strong enough to reverse the trend, so do not begin looking for a trend reversal just yet.
description: A trend-line break only counts as a meaningful reversal sign if the same countertrend move also closes beyond the moving average; a break that stays above (bull case) / below (bear case) the EMA should be ignored and the trader should keep taking only with-trend setups.

complexity.reason: depends on the trend-line primitive plus an EMA read

notes: Overlaps V02-17 CloseAboveEmaByMargin conceptually; kept as the AND of trend-line break and EMA break since the book states them as a joint requirement.

name: FailedPullbackToMovingAverage
quote: Failure of a pullback to reach the moving average. This indicates urgency and a strong trend.
description: In a bull trend, the current pullback bar's low stays above the moving average without touching it - a sign of a strong trend, used as a with-trend entry filter.
book_order_type: n/a (context filter, not itself an order)

complexity.reason: needs the 20-bar EMA (moving average) primitive maintained bar to bar

notes: movingAverage is the standard 20-bar EMA primitive defined in earlier chapters; not redefined here.

name: SurrogateMovingAverageFinerTimeframe
quote: You actually need to plot a 90 bar moving average on the 1 minute chart as a surrogate for the 5 minute 20 bar moving average... use a 90 bar moving average... which is very close to the 5 minute 20 bar moving average.
description: If the strategy's bar series is the finer of two nested timeframes (e.g. 1 minute standing in for 5 minute), use an EMA length equal to the coarser timeframe's EMA length times the timeframe ratio, minus a small correction (90 rather than 100 for a 5x ratio and a 20-bar EMA), then take a with-trend high1/low1 or high2/low2 setup at that average, risking only the height of the (smaller) signal bar.
pseudocode: low[0] <= surrogateMovingAverage[0] + toleranceTicks * tickSize && close[0] > open[0]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the high of the moving-average-touch signal bar

complexity.reason: an EMA maintained bar to bar with a specific length correction, combined with an existing moving-average-touch/high1-2 entry primitive

notes: This only requires a single bar series at the finer resolution (1 minute) with a differently-sized EMA - it does not require the engine to hold two simultaneous timeframes at once.
surrogateEmaLength = 90 is Brooks's specific correction for a 5x ratio and a 20-bar EMA (not simply 5x20=100); the general formula would need re-deriving for other ratios.

name: PriceLevelTouchRequirement
quote: When the market gets within a tick or so of a magnet, traders do not feel confident about the test unless the market gets that extra tick and actually touches the magnet. Until that happens, they usually will not aggressively trade it as a completed pullback.
description: Primitive: a significant price level (a magnet - moving average, prior swing extreme, round number) counts as tested only once price actually trades to or through it; a near-approach that falls short by any margin does not count.
pseudocode: touchesLevelAsSupport(level, marginTicks) = low[0] <= level + marginTicks * tick

complexity.reason: a single price-vs-level comparison with a tick margin

notes: Used via depends_on by V16-03; also generalizes the 'perfect breakout test' idea in V16-04 (a near-miss, the opposite polarity of this touch requirement).

name: EmaFlatFilter
quote: If it is a doji in the middle of a tight trading range from the final hour of yesterday and the moving average is flat, the odds favor a trading range day.
description: Shared primitive: the EMA has moved less than a small tick threshold over the last N bars -- 'the moving average is flat', used to reinforce a trading-range-day read.

complexity.reason: a difference of two EMA readings compared to a tick threshold

notes: Composes with FirstBarDojiImpliesTwoSidedDay (VP3-04) and yesterday's-closing-range tests to reproduce the book's full first-bar read.
chapter_title: Part III: The First Hour (The Opening Range) (introduction)

name: SteepEmaSlopeSellOffReversal
quote: Whenever the moving average is as steeply up as it was yesterday, any strong sell-off below it will almost always be followed by a tradable rally back up.
description: If the EMA had a steep up-slope in a recent session and price makes a strong sell-off below the current EMA, expect (and enter on) a reversal rally back up.
book_order_type: stop one tick above the reversal bar's high (long) / below its low (short)

complexity.reason: combines an EMA-slope measurement from a prior session with a same-day distance-below-EMA test and a reversal-bar test; the specific thresholds are not given by Brooks

notes: Composes with EmaFlatFilter (VP3-05) as the opposite-slope case (steep vs. flat).

name: GapProxyByFirstBarVsEma
quote: If the first bar is entirely above the moving average, think of the open as a gap up. If the first bar is entirely below the moving average, assume that the market is gapping down.
description: Context filter classifying the open as a bullish (bearish) gap day when the first bar of the session sits entirely above (below) the EMA, used when the actual gap versus yesterday's close is ambiguous.

complexity.reason: session-boundary primitive plus an EMA comparison

notes: This is a stated proxy for an actual open-vs-yesterday's-close gap test, which is simpler and mechanizable directly on daily bars (see GapUpOnOpen-style rules mined from chapter 20).
chapter_title: Patterns Related to Yesterday: Breakouts, Breakout Pullbacks, and Failed Breakouts

name: ExtendedGapBarStreakPredictsEmaTouch
quote: if you tested back over the past 10 or 20 years, you would find that more than 95 percent of the time when there were 30 or more consecutive gap bars, the market came back and touched the moving average within 10 bars.
description: After an extended streak of consecutive same-side moving-average gap bars (about 30 or more, well beyond the ordinary 20-bar 'strong trend' threshold), expect the market to touch the moving average again within about 10 bars; usable as a countertrend fade entry on a marginal new extreme, or as a profit-taking cue for an existing with-trend position.
pseudocode: consecutiveGapBars(direction) >= extremeGapBarStreak && close[0] > high[1] -> enter countertrend short at next bar's open, expecting a touch of ema[0] within touchWindowBars
book_order_type: buy/sell the option (or, mechanized here, enter the underlying) on a stop one tick beyond the prior bar's extreme, mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open

complexity.reason: builds on a persistent moving-average-gap-bar streak counter and adds a forward-looking timing window and probability claim, both of which need a separate lookback to instantiate as a coded rule

notes: Builds on reference/brooks/mined/reversals/00_front_matter.json's V00-14 TwentyMovingAverageGapBars (which flags a 20-bar streak as a strong-trend signal); this raises the threshold to 30 and adds the specific book-cited mean-reversion timing (~95% touch the EMA within 10 bars over the book's own 10-20 year lookback).

This chapter is 'Options' and is almost entirely about option mechanics (spreads, premium decay, implied volatility, open interest, skew, earnings catalysts) that the engine has no data for; only a handful of bar-based ideas are recorded here as candidates, and the bulk of the chapter is grouped into a few brief rejected entries below rather than itemized line by line.

name: MovingAverageGapBar
quote: the bar 25 first moving average gap bar in the larger bull trend, which is often a buy signal
description: The first bar in a trend that gaps to the opposite side of the 20-bar EMA (e.g. the first bear-trend bar whose entire range is below the EMA) after a run of bars mostly on the trend side, signaling renewed momentum; entry is one tick beyond that bar in the trend direction.
pseudocode: allBarsAbove = high[1] > ema[1] // prior N bars mostly above ema; gapBar = high[0] < ema[0] && close[0] < open[0]

complexity.reason: EMA comparison plus a short run-state check on prior bars

name: QuietFlagLimitEntryAtMA
quote: Buying at or below the prior bar on a limit order in a quiet bull flag at the moving average.
description: In an established trend, when price is consolidating quietly (small overlapping bars, low range) at the moving average, rest a limit order at or below the prior bar's low (above the prior bar's high for shorts) rather than waiting for a stop entry.
book_order_type: resting limit order at/below the prior bar's low

complexity.reason: an EMA-distance test plus a below-average-range 'quiet' test

chapter_title: The Best Trades: Putting It All Together

name: MajorityBarsOnMASideFilter
quote: They should look to buy only when the market is mostly above the moving average and sell when most of the recent bars are below the moving average.
description: Only allow long entries when a clear majority of the last N bars have closed above the 20-bar EMA (mirrored: shorts only when a majority closed below).
pseudocode: countBarsAbove = countBars(close[i] > ema[i], lookback); countBarsAbove >= majorityFraction*lookback

complexity.reason: a window loop counting bars against an EMA compared to a fraction threshold

chapter_title: The Best Trades: Putting It All Together

name: FlatEmaTightRangeBarbwireAvoidance
quote: Beginners should avoid trading in the middle of the day when the market is in the middle of a day's range, especially if the moving average is relatively flat and the trading range is tight and has prominent tails (barbwire).
description: Avoid entering trades when the moving average is relatively flat, the recent range is tight, and the bars have prominent tails (a 'barbwire' condition), especially around midday.
pseudocode: isMidDay(0) && abs(ema[0] - ema[emaLookback]) <= flatEmaThreshold && (highest(high, rangeLookback) - lowest(low, rangeLookback)) <= tightRangeThreshold && avgTailFraction(rangeLookback) >= tailFractionThreshold -> block entries

complexity.reason: composite of an EMA-slope test, a range-width test, and an average-tail-length test, each needing an instrument-specific threshold; not a single computation

notes: All numeric thresholds are inventions; the book only gives the qualitative description ('relatively flat', 'tight', 'prominent tails').

Overlaps with reference/brooks/mined/reversals/11_key_times_of_the_day.json's MidDayLowProbabilityWindowFilter; this candidate adds the explicit flat-EMA + barbwire composite test on top of a time-of-day gate, so the dedup pass should compare rather than assume duplication.

name: SevenOfTenBarsAboveEmaBlocksShorts
quote: If seven of the past 10 bars are mostly above the moving average, do not look to short. Instead, only look to buy. If seven of the past 10 bars are mostly below the moving average, do not look to buy. Instead, only look to short.
description: Block short entries when at least 7 of the last 10 bars closed above the moving average (only longs are permitted); block long entries when at least 7 of the last 10 bars closed below the moving average (only shorts are permitted).
pseudocode: countIf(close[i] > ema[i], i, 0, lookback - 1) >= minBarsAboveEma -> block short entries

complexity.reason: a rolling count of bars closing above/below their own EMA value over a fixed window; the EMA itself is a standard indicator, and the counting is a simple loop

name: MovingAverageGapBarPrimitive
quote: moving average gap bar (gap bar) A bar that does not touch the moving average. The space between the bar and the moving average is the gap.
description: Primitive: bar 0 does not touch the EMA -- its low is entirely above it (bull gap bar) or its high entirely below it (bear gap bar).

complexity.reason: needs an EMA state variable

notes: Existing rule tests close against a simple average; this tests low/high (bar entirely clear) against Brooks's EMA.

name: TwentyMovingAverageGapBarsStreak
quote: 20 moving average gap bars Twenty or more consecutive bars that have not touched the moving average. Once the market finally touches the moving average, it usually creates a setup for a test of the trend's extreme.
description: At least N consecutive prior bars were all moving-average gap bars on the same side -- a sign-of-strength flag (also listed among the Introduction's bull-trend characteristics, p57) feeding T07-40's gap-bar buy.
pseudocode: for k in 1..streakBars: MovingAverageGapBarPrimitive[k] holds on the same side

complexity.reason: EMA plus a run-length counter

name: NoOppositeSideClosesFilter
quote: No two consecutive trend bar closes occur on the opposite side of the moving average.
description: In the last N bars, no two consecutive closes sit on the opposite side of the EMA from the trend direction: an always-in confirmation filter.
pseudocode: !(exists k in 0..lookback-2: close[k] < ema[k] && close[k+1] < ema[k+1])

complexity.reason: EMA plus a two-bar scan over a window

name: BarsSinceEmaTouchExtreme
quote: if the daily SPY is in a bull channel and it has not touched the moving average for 45 days and it has only done that once in the past 10 years, the current behavior is extremely unusual.
description: Context filter: the market has gone at least N bars without the price touching its EMA -- an extreme extension that institutions view as due for a pullback to the average.

complexity.reason: needs an EMA plus a persistent bars-since-touch counter

notes: Brooks's example is the daily SPY specifically; the mechanism generalizes to any bar size.

name: MarketInTrend
quote: the market often trends for a protracted time with only small pullbacks... An important point to remember is that the market constantly exhibits inertia and tends to continue to do what is has just been doing.
description: Primitive: approximate 'the market is in a trend' (bull side) as a net directional move over the last trendBars bars where most of those bars agree with the direction (inertia). No EMA is introduced until later chapters, so this uses only net close change plus a majority-of-bars count.

complexity.reason: 'the market is in a trend' is a design decision; net-move-plus-majority-count is one workable proxy, not Brooks's own test

notes: Later chapters define this via the 20-bar EMA; this chapter has not introduced the EMA yet.

name: Ema20
quote: a market that has been in a trading range day until it reverses up strongly to just above the moving average ... Bull flags just above the moving average where there are three or more large bars that mostly overlap are usually traps.
description: Primitive: the 20-bar exponential moving average of closes; 'above the EMA' = close[0] > ema[0].

complexity.reason: needs an EMA state variable

notes: Chapter does not repeat the '20' figure explicitly (it says only 'the moving average'); 20 is the corpus-standard EMA length used elsewhere in this book.

name: BullFlagOverlapTrapFilter
quote: Bull flags just above the moving average where there are three or more large bars that mostly overlap are usually traps. The same is true for a bear flag just below the moving average where there are three or more large bear bars that largely overlap.
description: Block a with-trend long entered above a signal bar sitting just above the EMA when that signal bar and the two bars before it are large and mostly overlapping (a common bull-flag trap, mirrored below the EMA for bear flags).
pseudocode: !(close[0] > ema[0] && range(0) >= largeMultiple * avgRange(rangeLookback) && overlap(0, 1) >= trapOverlapFrac * range(1) && overlap(1, 2) >= trapOverlapFrac * range(2))

complexity.reason: EMA plus a multi-bar overlap test

notes: Brooks estimates about a 60 percent trap rate for this pattern (p122's similar flag example uses the same figure).

name: Ema20
quote: if there is a strong bull trend and at least 20 consecutive bars have been above the moving average, and the market drifts sideways to the rising moving average, look to buy the close of the first small bear trend bar.
description: Primitive: the 20-bar exponential moving average of closes; 'above the EMA' = close[0] > ema[0].

complexity.reason: needs an EMA state variable

notes: Same primitive as T07-06, defined independently here per the one-primitive-per-chapter rule.

name: ConsecutiveBarsBeyondEma
quote: at least 20 consecutive bars have been above the moving average
description: Context filter: the last establishedBars bars all closed above (bull) / below (bear) the 20-bar EMA -- an established with-trend run.
pseudocode: for k in 0..establishedBars-1: close[k] > ema[k] -> allAboveEma; filter passes when allAboveEma

complexity.reason: a 20-bar window over an EMA state variable

name: MovingAverageGapBarPullbackEntry
quote: look to buy the close of the first small bear trend bar with a close that is only a tick or two below the moving average. Also, look to buy above its high.
description: After an established bull run (bars closing above the EMA for a while), buy the close of the first small counter-colored (bear) trend bar that closes within a tick or two of the EMA -- a with-trend continuation entry on the pullback's exhaustion.
pseudocode: ConsecutiveBarsBeyondEma[1] (bull) && TrendBar[0] (bear) && abs(close[0] - ema[0]) <= gapTicks * tick
book_order_type: buy at the market on the bar's close, and also place a buy stop one tick above its high

complexity.reason: combines the EMA state variable with a small counter-colored-bar test

notes: This is the '20 gap bar' setup Brooks refers to repeatedly through the chapter's chart discussions (e.g. pp. 142-143, 165); the general EMA-gap-bar idea is also referenced from T07-06/T07-08.

name: Ema20
quote: There was a two-legged pullback to the moving average at bar 3, which was also a 20 gap bars short setup.
description: Primitive: the 20-bar exponential moving average of closes; 'above the EMA' = close[0] > ema[0].

complexity.reason: needs an EMA state variable

notes: CloseAboveAverage uses a simple average; Brooks uses the 20 EMA.

name: MovingAverageGapBarBuy
quote: The bar before bar 3 was a moving average gap bar buy setup in a strong trend, so buying above it, even with an outside up bar, was a good trade.
description: In a strong bull trend the prior bar is entirely below the EMA (its high is below the EMA, leaving a gap); this bar closes above the gap bar's high: buy. Brooks's '20 gap bars' is the same idea with at least 20 prior bars entirely on one side of the EMA.
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the gap bar's high

complexity.reason: EMA plus a streak counter of bars on one side of it

notes: p190: 'a 20 gap bars short setup' at a two-legged pullback to the moving average.
p197: 'The move down to a 20 gap bars setup almost always breaks a trend line, and the move up from the bar usually tests the high of the trend'.

name: TargetPriorTrendHighAfterGapBar
quote: the move up from the bar usually tests the high of the trend with either a higher high or a lower high. If there is then a reversal down, it usually leads to at least two legs lasting at least 10 bars
description: After a moving-average-gap-bar long, take profit when the bar's high reaches the highest high of the N bars before entry (the test of the trend high).
book_order_type: limit sell at the prior trend high

complexity.reason: highest over a window anchored at entry via BarsSinceEntry

notes: The follow-on 'reversal from the test leads to two legs / 10 bars' is a countertrend entry idea for the reversals book.

name: FailedBreakoutAtEma
quote: The market ... broke above the bear channel into yesterday's close, but the breakout failed at the moving average, setting up a short.
description: LONG form (mirror): in a bull context (close above the EMA for the last N bars) the bar dips through the EMA (low below it) but closes back above it — a failed breakout at the moving average. Buy at the next open.
pseudocode: low[0] < ema && close[0] > ema && countTrue(close[i] > ema[i] for i in 1..priorBars) >= priorBars where ema = xaverage(close, emaLength)
book_order_type: buy stop above the signal bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: EMA plus a window of EMA relations

notes: Brooks's original is a bear-channel breakout above that failed at the EMA; the channel part is dropped here.

name: MovingAverage20Ema
quote: The moving average therefore contains the trend, and functions like the lower line of a channel.
description: Primitive: Brooks's 'moving average' is the 20-bar EMA of closes. Defined once here as a named value ma = ema(close, maLength) that other candidates reference.

complexity.reason: an EMA carries state between bars

notes: Existing CloseAboveAverage is a simple average; Brooks uses an exponential one.

name: MovingAverageTouch
quote: When a bull trend is strong, traders will buy tests of the moving average, like at bars 13 and 15.
description: The bar's low touches or penetrates the EMA (within tolTicks) while the close holds above it; buy at the next open. p275 (no-space page): some bulls used a limit order one tick above the EMA in case the market only touched it.
pseudocode: low[0] <= ma + tolTicks * tickSize && close[0] > ma
book_order_type: limit order at or one tick above the EMA

complexity.reason: EMA state

name: High2AtMovingAverageWithBullSignalBar
quote: The most reliable buy signal will be a high 2 with a bull signal bar at the moving average where the entry is not too close to the top of the channel.
description: Composite: in a bull channel, a high 2 whose signal bar is a bull bar touching the EMA, with the entry far enough below the channel line. Brooks's 'perfect' beginner channel trade.
book_order_type: buy stop above the signal bar

complexity.reason: inherits the channel line from T15-22

name: MovingAverageGapBar
quote: Bar 7 was a second-entry moving average gap bar short in a bear trend, which often leads to the final leg in the bear trend before a larger reversal develops.
description: Long side: in a bull trend (close above EMA for most of the last trendBars), a bar forms entirely below the EMA (high[0] < ma): a moving average gap bar. Buy when the next bar closes above that bar's high. Brooks prefers the second entry.
pseudocode: high[1] < ma[1] && close[0] > high[1] && countBarsAboveMa(trendBars) >= trendBars * trendFraction
book_order_type: buy stop above the gap bar (second entry preferred)

complexity.reason: EMA plus a window count

notes: The full '20 gap bars' setup (a run of 20 bars not touching the EMA) is defined in the chapter 16/17 files.

name: PullbackStaysAboveMovingAverageForLongs
quote: There was a bear channel and the market was spending most of the day below the moving average.
description: Trend-side filter: the fraction of the last windowBars closing above the EMA is at least minFraction; when true trade the long side only (mirror for shorts).
pseudocode: count over i in 0..windowBars-1 of (close[i] > ma[i]) >= minFraction * windowBars

complexity.reason: EMA plus a window count

notes: A cheap proxy for the always-in direction (T15-09).

name: TwentyGapBarPullbackSetup
quote: both days were strong trend days with one extreme near the open and then no moving average pullback for over two hours (20 gap bar pullback setups).
description: Shared primitive: a run of at least gapBarsThreshold consecutive bars all staying on one side of the EMA (never touching it), followed by the first bar to touch/cross back to it -- the '20 gap bars' pullback entry. Buy the first touch of the EMA after such a run.
pseudocode: barsSinceLastEmaTouch(maLength) >= gapBarsThreshold && low[0] <= ma && close[0] > ma
book_order_type: buy stop above the touch bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: needs an EMA plus a bars-since counter of how long price has avoided the average, in addition to the fixed-offset touch test

name: OpeningSelloffToHigherTimeframeEMA
quote: The opens often have sharp sell-offs that trap bulls out and bears in but usually find support at the 15 or 60 minute moving average or at some other support level
description: Day after a strong bull trend day: buy the early sell-off when a bar's low touches the higher-time-frame moving average (approximated on the trading chart by a longer EMA, e.g. 20-bar EMA of 60-minute bars = 240 bars of 5-minute) within the first N bars of the session.

complexity.reason: EMA plus session-open bar counting plus the prior-day flag

name: NewHighAfterTwoSidedRallyIsShort
quote: If a rally to test the high has several small pullbacks within the leg up, with lots of overlapping bars, several bear bodies, and big tails on the tops of the bars, and most of the bull trend bars are weak, then the market is becoming increasingly two-sided.
description: Countertrend setup (written as the mirrored short-to-long form): when the rally into a new high shows two-sided signs (bear bodies, overlap, upper tails, weak bull bars) and, per p314, a prior pullback closed well below the EMA, the breakout above the old high is faded. Long form: fade a breakout below the old low after a two-sided sell-off.

complexity.reason: swing reference plus several window statistics and a failed-breakout test

name: TrendAgeBars

When true, new highs are shorting opportunities, not buys; as a long filter require it false. Mirror (p315): a strong rally above the bear trend line and EMA flips the bear.

name: FirstEmaPullbackThenTestOfHigh
quote: This first pullback to the moving average will usually be followed by a test of the high of the bull trend.
description: Exit: a long entered on the first pullback to the EMA after a very strong bull run takes profit when the high reaches the prior trend high (within tolerance); the rally may be the final one before a larger correction.
pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && enteredOnFirstEmaPullback && high[0] >= priorTrendHigh - tolAtr * atr

complexity.reason: needs the trend high remembered and the 'first' pullback state

name: MovingAverageGapBarEntry
quote: the bull trend was so strong that it was simply a 20 gap bar buy signal leading to a protracted channel up
description: Entry: in a bull trend that has held above the EMA for at least N bars, the first bar whose high is entirely below the EMA (a gap between bar and average) is the signal bar; buy when a following bar closes above its high.
pseudocode: barsAboveEmaBefore >= strongBars && high[1] < ema(close, emaLength)[1] && close[0] > high[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the gap bar high

complexity.reason: EMA plus a persistent count of bars above it
